links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and guideline adherence in simulated clinical setting versus licensing-exam performance
links.effect: LLMs did not accurately diagnose across all pathologies, performed significantly worse than physicians, followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and could not interpret laboratory results.
links.quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

links.outcome: LLM sensitivity to quantity and order of information and instruction following
links.effect: LLMs often failed to follow instructions and were sensitive to both the quantity and order of information provided.
links.quote: Furthermore, we move beyond diagnostic accuracy and demonstrate that they cannot be easily integrated into existing workflows because they often fail to follow instructions and are sensitive to both the quantity and order of information.

links.outcome: LLM adherence to diagnostic and treatment guidelines
links.effect: LLMs followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines.
links.quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

screen.reason: The study develops a simulation benchmark using 2,400 MIMIC cases to evaluate LLM clinical decision-making performance, workflow integration, guideline adherence, and safety risks, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
